newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to tender 19.8 pct Slavneft.
newsitem.headline: Russia to tender 19.8 pct Slavneft.

text.p: Russia will hold an investment tender for 19.8 percent of Russian-Belarussian oil company NGK Slavneft at the end of May or in June, Slavneft President Anatoly Fomin said on Wednesday.
Up to 15 percent of the company, whose main oil production unit is Megionneftegaz, will be available to foreign investors, he told a news conference.

Fomin gave no details of the tender terms. At an investment tender, bidders compete to offer investment in the company. They often have to take on company debts as well, while the stake being auctioned usually goes for a fixed price.

Russia sold 2.12 percent of Slavneft, or about 2.5 million shares, in December at 12,121 roubles per share. After the auction there was a 40-for-one share split, and the face value of shares is now one rouble. Capital is about 4.57 billion roubles.
The Russian government owns about 84 percent of Slavneft and the Belarussian government about nine percent.
Slavneft produced 12.9 million tonnes of oil in 1996, down from 13.2 million in 1995.
